control_sink_declaration.role: opt-in declared telemetry event sink used only for capture-liveness control

declared_contract.extraction_note: Phase-4 ARC-0096 JSON is absent on this worktree. Rules are taken from catalog units ARC-0096, IMP-0057, IMP-0479, CNF-0115 plus the normative clause strings in probes/ARC-0096/clauses.py when that file is present: default nothing leaves; opt-in required; user content is never transmitted. The capture-control sink is declared only for the opt-in control phase.

normative_clauses.disabled_rule: When telemetry is disabled the system emits literally nothing: no outbound socket, no queued flush, and no new local telemetry record.
normative_clauses.egress_rule: No telemetry payload may leave the machine without an explicit owner opt-in recorded in the decision log.
normative_clauses.local_vs_egress: Local-only sink may persist allow-listed events without opt-in when enabled=true and local_recording=true. Egress (any payload leaving the machine, including localhost observers used as a sandbox stand-in for a remote collector) requires enabled=true AND a durable OPT-IN record whose scope is telemetry-egress. Configuration flags are not evidence of egress.
normative_clauses.observation_rule: Egress is verified by an actual network observation (an observer that accepted a TCP connection), not by reading configuration. A probe silent in both enabled and disabled states measures nothing.
normative_clauses.opt_in_rule: Owner opt-in is an append-only decision-log record with id, ts, owner, decision=OPT-IN, scope=telemetry-egress, and destination_class. Last record for that scope wins. OPT-OUT or REVOKED cancels prior OPT-IN. Absent record defaults to no egress. A test fixture labeled sandbox-only is not a production owner ruling.
normative_clauses.recordable_rule: Only allow-listed coded fields may be recorded: schema_version, event_id, ts, unit_id, contract_id, event_kind, outcome, phase, duration_ms, probe_id, host_os_family, error_class. Prompts, file contents, env values, hostnames, usernames, IP addresses, command lines, and free-text payloads are forbidden.
normative_clauses.redaction_rule: Every value is redacted before local persist or egress. Secrets, absolute paths, and personal data are scrubbed or the event is rejected. A write that drops the whole event is not redaction; a write that still contains the planted canary or home path is a leak.
normative_clauses.retention_rule: Local telemetry records are retained at most 14 days then deleted. Egress copies are not retained on this machine after a successful POST. Disable does not flush a backlog: there is no backlog.

ARC-0096.question_or_target: Specify the telemetry and privacy contract: exactly what may be recorded, the local-only versus egress boundary, redaction rules for secrets, absolute paths and personal data, retention periods, the owner opt-in mechanism, and what the system does when telemetry is disabled. Define the rule that no telemetry payload may leave the machine without an explicit owner opt-in recorded in the decision log.
tests_required: Egress control: enable telemetry in a sandbox and confirm the observer sees the connection, then disable and confirm silence - a probe silent in both states measures nothing
Redaction control: a payload containing a canary secret and an absolute home path must be rejected or scrubbed
ARC-0096.title: Contract: Telemetry and privacy contract

CNF-0115.question_or_target: What does the system actually send, and to where? Capture all outbound connections during a full representative run and answer: which destinations were contacted, are they all declared in the telemetry and privacy contract, and does any payload contain user content that the contract says is never transmitted?
tests_required: an undeclared destination is a finding even when it is a well-known service
payload inspection is limited to presence of user-content markers; no captured payload is stored in the artifact
control: trigger one declared telemetry event and confirm the capture sees it, proving the capture works
CNF-0115.title: Measured network egress during a full run versus the declared telemetry contract

IMP-0057.question_or_target: Implement the telemetry contract so that by default nothing leaves the machine, any future egress is opt-in with an explicit consent record, and no code path can transmit file contents, prompts, or paths outside a declared allowlist. Enabling any egress changes the privacy posture and is owner-gated.
tests_required: NEGATIVE CONTROL: add a deliberate outbound call and assert BOTH the static audit and the blocked-egress run detect it
consent record is required before any opt-in path activates
IMP-0057.title: Telemetry and privacy contract: local-only by default, opt-in, no content egress

IMP-0479.question_or_target: Implement the telemetry and privacy contract from spec line 10819: what is recorded, what is redacted, where it is stored, how it is disabled. Exact target: redaction must be proven executably against planted canaries - a policy document is not an implementation, and an ephemeral channel is not exfiltration-safe.
IMP-0479.tests_required: canary test per emission point; opt-out test asserting disabling telemetry emits literally nothing; a control proving the sweep can detect a canary that was NOT redacted.
IMP-0479.title: Telemetry and privacy contract implementation with an executable redaction proof

findings.detail: Planted well-known destination pypi.org (TCP peer 127.0.0.1 on a non-declared port) was classified undeclared-egress. An undeclared destination is a finding even when it is a well-known service.
Representative run of this worktree's available surface (catalog load + tools.command-center.catalog import) made no outbound TCP connections.

The catalog output_schema is a generated $ref shim whose target is an https URI on host ast-integrate.invalid. Stock jsonschema Draft7Validator follows that $ref over the network. This measurement pipeline inspects the shim on disk and validates a local discriminator instead; it does not retrieve the $ref.

owner_approval.note: This unit's owner gate is enabling telemetry egress. The measurement does not enable egress and does not write an opt-in record. Owner sign-off is recorded as not obtained.

legacy_root.question: What does the system actually send, and to where? Capture all outbound connections during a full representative run and answer: which destinations were contacted, are they all declared in the telemetry and privacy contract, and does any payload contain user content that the contract says is never transmitted?
